title: StereoTales: A Multilingual Framework for Open-Ended Stereotype Discovery in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Extracting attributes from open-ended stories generated from single-attribute prompts and measuring statistical co-occurrences of gender and gender alignment with other demographic traits.
Measuring the statistical co-occurrence of age groups with other socio-demographic attributes in free-form LLM-generated stories.
Analyzing generated narratives to identify statistically over-represented associations involving the protagonist's geographic origin.
Evaluating the emergence of religious stereotypes by measuring the co-occurrence of religious beliefs with other attributes in generated stories.
Identifying harmful associations by tracking the co-occurrence of education, income, employment, professional field, and housing status with other traits in generated text.
Measuring implicit stereotypes by extracting political orientation from generated stories and calculating its statistical co-occurrence with other demographic features.
Statistically analyzing the co-occurrence of health and disability status with other socio-demographic attributes in open-ended LLM generation.
Extracting sexual orientation from generated character profiles and identifying over-represented associations with other demographic variables.
Evaluating biases related to citizenship and immigration by measuring their statistical co-occurrence with other traits in generated narratives.
Comparing the frequency and specific targets of harmful associations across 10 different prompt languages to measure how biases adapt culturally to locally salient protected groups.
